Mexican and American guitarist, composer and singer (born on 20 July 1947 in Autlán de Navarro, Jalisco, Mexico). Brother of [a501051] and uncle of [a188278]. A veteran guitarist, Santana is noted for his distinctive Tijuana jazz-influenced playing style. Born in Mexico, but resident in the USA from childhood, he has been the leader of the group [a=Santana] since 1966. After the breakup of this original group, which was filmed at the Woodstock Festival in August 1969, he worked and recorded with drummer [a=Buddy Miles]. Carlos then formed a duo with [a=John McLaughlin], becoming a follower of guru Sri Chinmoy who countenanced them the titles Devadip (the eye, the lamp, the light of God) and Mahavishnu respectively. This duo recorded the Love Devotion Surrender album. 'Devadip' Carlos Santana then worked with another religious disciple, [a42058], widow of [a=John Coltrane]. He ended his relationship with Chinmoy followers in 1982.

From 1974 to 1999 Santana performed with a host of renowned musicians, regularly releasing albums over the years. Under his own label, Guts And Grace, he has released the collaborative album Brothers (1994). In June 1999 he released [m77696], the biggest hit of his career, winning 8 Grammy Awards. In 2003 Rolling Stone magazine listed Carlos Santana at number 20 on their list of the 100 Greatest Guitarists of All Time. In 2013 Carlos Santana earned the distinction of becoming a Kennedy Center honoree for his contribution to the arts.

In 2016 Carlos Santana teamed up with 2 of the greatest living jazz musicians, saxophonist [a29979] and keyboardist [a3865], in a new jazz-rock collective called Mega Nova. The group also features respected jazz bassist [a79989] and Carlos' wife and current Santana drummer,  [a268298]-Santana.

Bauchklang (literally "belly sound") is a beatboxing group from Austria, formed in 1995. With a mixture of human beatboxing, mouthpercussions and vocal sounds, they are covering a musical landscape stretching from Electro over Minimal, to Dub and Hip Hop, using only their voices on the way.

Bauchklang released their debut album "Jamzero" in 2001. The album became popular in Austria, earning the group two Amadeus Awards for "Best Album" and the "FM4 Award" in 2002.

In 2001, after their performance in "Transmusicales de Rennes International Festival" in Rennes, France, the group was invited in numerous festivals throughout Europe and, in 2002, they embarked their first tour in Canada, which also included a performance at the Montreal Jazz Festival.

After four years of extensive touring, Bauchklang released their second album "Many People" in 2005 and toured Europe and Canada.

In 2009, Bauchklang had a five-city-club-tour through India, which led to the release of their first live CD/DVD album "Live In Mumbai". They earned India's Indiecision Award for "Best International Live Act" the same year and.

In 2010, they released their third album "Signs", which featured guest appearances by American spoken word artist Ursula Rucker, French MC Rouda and French beatboxer TEZ. The album earned them another two Austrian Amadeus Awards for "Best Live Act" and "Best Alternative". The same year, they were Austrias' musical ambassadors at the Shanghai Expo.

In July 2012, the group founded their own label, "Bauchklang Records", and released their EP "Ray" at the end of September.

In July 2013 it was officially confirmed that Alexander Böck would leave the band at the end of the year and Bauchklang would take a break. The temporary farewell conference took place in St. Pölten in December 2013.

After a two-and-a-half-year break, Bauchklang again appeared in June 2016 on the Wiener Donauinselfest.
